claims: The Artemis mission is NASA's Moon-to-Mars program.
The Artemis mission aims to establish a long-term human presence on the Moon for scientific discovery, economic development, and as a stepping stone for future human missions to Mars.
The Artemis mission involves returning astronauts including the first woman and person of color to the lunar surface.
The Artemis mission involves building the Gateway lunar space station.
The Artemis mission involves establishing a base camp.
Artemis I took place in 2022.
Artemis I successfully completed an uncrewed flight test.
Artemis I orbited the Moon with the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft.
Artemis II is planned for 2026.
Artemis II is a 10-day crewed mission to orbit the Moon.
Artemis II tests systems with astronauts on board.
Artemis III is planned for 2027/2028.
Artemis III aims to land astronauts near the lunar south pole.
Artemis III aims to achieve the first astronaut landing on the Moon since 1972.
Artemis III utilizes a commercial landing system.
Artemis IV and beyond focus on building the Gateway station in lunar orbit.
Artemis IV and beyond focus on developing a sustained human presence.
Space Launch System (SLS) is NASA's heavy-lift rocket designed to launch crew and cargo.
Orion Spacecraft is the capsule transporting astronauts to and from the Moon.
Gateway is a planned space station in lunar orbit acting as a hub for science and surface missions.
Human Landing System (HLS) consists of commercial vehicles such as SpaceX's Starship.
Human Landing System (HLS) is designed to land crews on the surface.
The Artemis program is supported by international partners including Canada (CSA), Europe (ESA), and Japan (JAXA), along with private companies.
